messages:
maya (DevEx): heads up — found a repro where generator streaming leaks goroutines when a ctx cancel happens right after the handshake completes
kai (SDK): ugh. can you paste the minimal repro?
maya (DevEx): yep. boiled it down to this:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
// simulate cancel right after handshake returns
cancel()
for {
    tok, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { break }
    // process tokens
}
```

maya (DevEx): behavior: the handshake completes (server accepts & allocates backend) then cancel triggers but Recv() blocks for ~30s and goroutines pile up in runtime.Client.readLoop
alex (Runtime): interesting — so the runtime didn't observe the ctx cancellation and kept the socket open? any logs from runtime?
maya (DevEx): grabbed logs, here's the snippet: `handshake ok -> input stream open -> ctx canceled -> no close req until token deadline`
irene (SRE): could this be auth retry/backoff holding the connection? we recently changed transient auth refresh to retry inline for generator handshakes
kai (SDK): that rings a bell — the SDK's generator.Stream handshake uses a separate http request and then upgrades to a websocket-like stream. If the upgrade path doesn't propagate ctx cancellation into the underlying transport cancel, Recv can block waiting on read.
kai (SDK): quick hypothesis: our handshake path cancels the context on the initial request, but after the server returns 101/upgrade we spawn a goroutine that uses a different context without cancel propagation.
maya (DevEx): workaround for now: explicit `stream.Close()` after cancel in sample app fixes leak. but users won't know that during onboarding
alex (Runtime): patch idea: make runtime accept a cancel during post-upgrade token processing and send a close frame. Also add a small state machine test for handshake-cancel race
kai (SDK): on SDK side i'll add a defensive `ctx` wrapper so the read loop selects on both `ctx.Done()` and socket read. also add a unit test reproducing the race.
irene (SRE): can we add an e2e test to CI that cancels within 10ms of handshake success to catch regressions? ci-bot can run it in the matrix with linux/golang-latest
ci-bot: queued job: `generator-handshake-cancel-e2e` on linux/golang-latest (matrix run id 5421)
maya (DevEx): also propose we ship a small sample app change in onboarding: show `defer stream.Close()` and note `ctx` cancel semantics in the tutorial. New users hit this in workshops.
kai (SDK): will open two PRs: one in sdk (defensive select + test) and one in samples (doc + example). linking them here when ready.
maya (DevEx): thanks — ping me when PRs are up and i'll add a short blurb to the quickstart for generator ergonomics. also we should add a one-liner in the generator docs about handshake vs stream lifecycle and best-practices for cancel.
alex (Runtime): i'll prototype runtime fix this afternoon and we can coordinate a canary deploy to dedicated infra.
maya (DevEx): filing a small follow-up ticket for docs + sample app: https://redwood.internal/issue/RI-8342 (note: internal link)
kai (SDK): PRs: sdk#2148, samples#556 — added tests and example. leaving TODO to improve error on cancel to make it more obvious to users.
maya (DevEx): awesome. closing the loop here — will add a short note in the weekly devex digest once canary looks good. :thumbsup:
